subject: Proposal: split-year billing + flexible ramp window for Crestline renewal
messages:
From: Alice Park <alice.park@crestlinehealth.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com
Cc: tom.nguyen@crestlinehealth.com, procurement@crestlinehealth.com
Date: 2027-06-20T09:12:00Z
Subject: Renewal timing + FY split question

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the worksheet you shared during the call this morning. We have two internal asks before we can move to draft: 

1) Can Redwood split the first year invoice across our FY boundary? Our fiscal year ends 2027-09-30, and procurement prefers a 60/40 split for the first-year committed payment.
2) We also need a more explicit ramp window. Our product team expects usage to ramp over 3 quarters, but finance is asking for a shorter declared ramp (2 quarters) to recognise cost.

Can you propose a variant that supports a split invoice + a flexible ramp window we can agree on?

Appreciate it,
Alice

--
Alice Park
Head of Cloud Ops, Crestline Health
alice.park@crestlinehealth.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

From: soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Park <alice.park@crestlinehealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com, priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-06-22T13:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal timing + FY split question

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear asks. Attaching two artifacts: (1) a split-billing proposal that shows 60/40 invoicing for year one with amortized recognition for Redwood, and (2) a ramp schedule that provides both a 2-quarter and a 3-quarter option so you can pick. Key points up front: 

- We can support a 60/40 invoice split for the initial committed payment with an accounting note that Redwood will amortize revenue over the 12-month term (this is standard).
- For ramping, we propose a conservative plan (2-quarter declared ramp) and an operational true-up at quarter 3 if usage exceeds the declared ramp thresholds. That preserves Crestline's finance requirements while giving your product team room to scale.
- We can include a one-time Ops credit (USD 15k) to cover migration and extra support during the first 90 days; that credit will be applied on the second invoice.

If that sounds acceptable, I'll circulate a short amendment (no change to the base unit pricing or SLOs) and loop in Legal for a DocuSign-ready redline.

Attachments: crestline-proposal-split-billing-v2.pdf; crestline-ramp-schedule.xlsx

Best,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com | +1 (628) 555-0199

From: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Cc: priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-06-23T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal timing + FY split question

Looping in pricing/legal notes. A couple internal items to confirm before we send: 

- Revenue recognition: accounting confirmed amortization is fine, but Finance needs the 60/40 invoice schedule documented in the amendment so Crestline's AP has a PO match.
- Ops credit: confirm whether the credit is applied as an invoice line item or as a usage token credit. Prefer invoice line for clarity.
- Auto-renew: Alice asked earlier about auto-renew language. Recommend standard auto-renew with 30-day opt-out window; if Crestline needs a hard opt-in, we should surface that as a commercial concession.

Karthik, can you flag any infra or capacity commit implications if we accept a 2-quarter declared ramp with a Q3 true-up? Priyom, please draft the amendment stub we can send to Crestline (simple 1-2 page).

-Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Head of Renewals | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

From: karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com
Cc: priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-06-24T15:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal timing + FY split question

Quick infra note: a declared 2-quarter ramp with a potential Q3 true-up is manageable but we should set explicit throttles/fallbacks. Proposed technical guardrails: 

- Soft cap: baseline throughput for the first 90 days set to current committed tokens; automatic burst allowance of +35% for any 7-day window if downstream metrics (latency/error-rate) remain within SLOs.
- True-up trigger: if 7-day rolling consumption > 120% of declared baseline for two consecutive weeks, the system flags for an immediate scale event and Procurement is notified for true-up billing.
- If Crestline prefers a hard cap, that reduces risk but will require a short lag for scaling (24-72 hours to spin extra pools depending on capacity).

I'll add these guardrails to the amendment language as a short Operational Addendum.

-Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

From: soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Park <alice.park@crestlinehealth.com>, procurement@crestlinehealth.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com, priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-06-30T18:04:00Z
Subject: Proposed amendment and next steps (DocuSign link)

Hi Alice — attaching a short amendment that incorporates: (1) the 60/40 first-year invoice split; (2) a declared 2-quarter ramp with a Q3 operational true-up; (3) USD 15k Ops credit applied as a line-item on invoice #2; and (4) standard auto-renew language with a 30-day opt-out. Karthik also added the operational guardrails referenced above.

Please review the amendment and the ramp schedule. If this aligns with procurement, sign via DocuSign here: https://www.docusign.com/crestline/ds12345. Once signed, Legal will countersign and we will schedule the onboarding kickoff.

If procurement needs the Ops credit to be a token rather than invoice credit, call me and we can switch it, but invoice line is cleaner for your AP.

Thanks — excited to keep Crestline moving forward.

Best,
Soojin

Attachments: crestline-proposal-split-billing-v2.pdf; crestline-ramp-schedule.xlsx
